The warrior reaches the door by first removing the two dragons that threaten its route, then using the last dragon's breath to kill the goblin beside the door.

1. Walk to (14,10) and push dragon #19 north to (14,8). Its breath kills goblin #12 and clears row 9.
2. Walk to (9,11) and push dragon #2 east along row 11 until it drowns at (16,11). Its breath on the way kills goblin #21 and dragon #19.
3. Walk to (8,9) and push dragon #1 south twice to (8,12), then west of it at (7,12).
4. Push dragon #1 east along row 12 to (12,12). On the way its breath kills goblin #4, dragon #20, and then goblin #3, which was next to the door.
5. Walk south through the open gates (11,13) to (11,18). No goblin is orthogonally adjacent to the door any more, and no breath line crosses the path.

I couldn't find a winning sequence, so I'm not going to submit a guess as a solution.

Move 43 failed because the bridge gates at (11,15) and (11,16) are water while any monster is alive. The gates are inverted, so they stay open while monsters live. The warrior can only walk on them after every monster is dead, and the level has 18 monsters: 14 goblins and 4 dragons.

Some of those monsters sit in rooms the warrior can never reach. Only dragon breath can kill them, and each dragon faces a fixed direction. Working through a sequence, I kept running into conflicts: a dragon's breath line runs through the cells the warrior or another dragon must pass. I could not find an ordering that clears all 18 monsters and then lets the warrior reach the door.

I also made an error in my earlier plan by using the first dragon to clear the south goblins and then drowning it. That left the top and east goblins with no dragon that could reach them.

The opening below is valid, but it does not win:

<moves>RRRDDDLU</moves>
